picks.file: Wahre Contrafactur der Statt Elbing wie dieselbe von Königl. May zu Schweden etc. befestigt worden. Anno 1626 - M. Merian fecit - btv1b53235801w (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view with the Swedish fortifications of 1626, etching
picks.why: sharp first state of the plate; old town, St. Nicholas tower and the Elbing river clear; title and key trimmed

picks.what: View of the city, engraving in Christoph Hartknoch, Alt und Neues Preussen
picks.why: true prospect with St. Nicholas and the other church towers labeled; key at the bottom trimmed

notes: #1: the title gives 1626, the year the Swedes fortified the town; BnF dates this print 1635 and Merian published it in the early 1630s, hence ‘about 1630’. It shows the town’s state, not a siege, so not marked as an event. #3 is another copy of the same state with library stamps; #4 and #6 are a later state with a second title line about Charles XII taking the town in 1703; #2 is the blank reverse. #5: Commons says ‘published in Christoph Hartknoch’s monograph of 1648’, but Hartknoch was born in 1644; his Alt und Neues Preussen appeared in 1684, so 1648 looks like swapped digits — please confirm the year.
